attempts.summary: Set up PostgreSQL 13 streaming replication across node1 (initial primary), node2 and node3 (standbys) on AlmaLinux 9, using pg_basebackup -R with a dedicated replicator role (SCRAM-SHA-256) and opened firewalld port 5432. Demonstrated failover: stopped node1's postgres, promoted node2 via pg_ctl promote (timeline advanced to 2), repointed node3's primary_conninfo to node2, verified zero committed-data loss (all pre-failover rows present on both survivors, new writes accepted by node2). Rebuilt node1 from a fresh pg_basebackup against node2 and brought it back online as a standby of the new primary, restoring the 3-node topology (node2 primary, node1/node3 standbys) with all historical rows intact. Then ran the mandatory node-restart protocol on all three nodes one at a time (node1, node3, node2/primary last) using systemctl reboot backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnect; confirmed each node's boot_id changed, PostgreSQL came back active, replication/recovery role was correct, and a final write on the primary replicated to both standbys after every node had been restarted.
